item.title: Is Sparkling Water The New “Brain Fuel” for Gamers?
item.description: Ditch the sugar. New research shows that the simple fizz of sparkling water can keep your brain sharp and your "gaming fouls" low during three-hour esports sessions.

item.title: Low-Dose Lithium May Shield Against Verbal Memory Loss
item.description: A new pilot study reveals that low-dose lithium may act as a neuroprotective shield, slowing verbal memory loss in patients at risk for Alzheimer’s.

item.title: Brain’s Family Tree: A New Theory of Neural Self-Organization
item.description: A new theory of brain development suggests that neurons find their place by staying near their relatives, rather than following distant chemical signals.

item.title: Why Socializing Loses to Alcohol in Addiction
item.description: New research reveals that activity in the anterior insula primes the brain to choose alcohol over social interaction, offering a new target for addiction treatment.

item.title: Beyond Weight Loss: Ozempic Linked to Migraine Reduction
item.description: Unexpected relief. New research shows that patients taking GLP-1 drugs for diabetes or weight loss also experience fewer emergency room visits and need fewer medications for their chronic migraines.

item.title: Trick the Brain, Taste the Reward: How Expectations Rewrite Sweetness
item.description: Expectation is the secret ingredient. New neuroimaging research reveals that believing a drink contains sugar can "supercharge" the brain's reward response to artificial sweeteners.

item.title: High-Speed Eye Tests Detect “Invisible” Brain Injuries
item.description: Scientists discover that the brain's ability to track movement remains impaired for decades after a concussion, revealing the long-term reality of head injuries.

item.title: Why Some COVID Patients Lose Taste for Years
item.description: Scientists discover a molecular "amplifier" defect in the taste buds of long-COVID patients, explaining why some flavors disappear while others remain.

item.title: AI Fails to Find Link Between Brain Structure and Navigation Skills
item.description: Advanced AI tools fail to find a link between the physical structure of the brain and navigation ability, challenging decades of neuroscientific assumptions.

item.title: Home Drinking Water May Impact Parkinson’s Risk
item.description: New research reveals that drinking water from modern, shallow groundwater systems is associated with a significantly higher risk of Parkinson’s disease.
